construct: Loss of the apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb impairs sodium chloride reabsorption, reduces the lumen-positive potential that normally drives paracellular calcium reabsorption, activates renin-aldosterone signaling, and produces hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with hypercalciuria.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with high renin/aldosterone, hypercalciuria/nephrocalcinosis, and biallelic SLC12A1 variants identifies type 1 Bartter syndrome; SLC12A1 encodes the thick-ascending-limb apical NKCC2 cotransporter.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: NCC loss causes Gitelman with hypocalciuria; ENaC gain causes Liddle with suppressed renin/aldosterone; generalized Na-K ATPase or proximal SGLT defects do not reproduce the SLC12A1 loop-diuretic-like phenotype.
